answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut is severe and non-negotiable. The assembly line's 94% utilization leaves minimal buffer for supply disruption, making single-vendor switches or second-sourcing high-risk in the 14-day window. Renewing with the incumbent at current terms forfeits margin recovery opportunity. Deferral is not viable given the hard deadline. Negotiating terms leverages the fact that the incumbent has already demonstrated willingness to move on both price and payment terms (memory_c4), and we have evidence that multi-year commitments unlock volume pricing (memory_c6). Verification of memory_c2 (quick onboarding and accurate invoicing from low-cost vendors) and memory_c4 (benchmarking power and incumbent flexibility) will confirm whether aggressive negotiation is realistic within 14 days. A standard experiment scale allows us to anchor on aggressive cost targets while preserving fallback to renewal if negotiations stall, minimizing delivery risk during the high-utilization period.
